newsitem.title: UK: IBCA ups short-, long-term ratings on Next.
newsitem.headline: IBCA ups short-, long-term ratings on Next.

text.p: IBCA, the European rating agency, said on Thursday it had upgraded the long- and short-term ratings of Next Plc to A minus and A1 from BBB plus and A2 respectively.

"Having restructured its business to concentrate in its successful Next retail and Next Directory operations, Next plc, a leading UK high street fashion retailer, has put the problems of the early 1990s behind it," IBCA said in a statement.

"Net cash of 170 million stg at financial-year-end 1996 and strong operating cashflow underpin the group's robust financial profile, with coverages now amongst the highest of those retailers rated by IBCA," it added.
It said Next's strategy continued to focus on building loyalty to the Next brand, enhanced by closer links between the Retail and Directory operations.
This, in turn, would provide economies of scale in both purchasing and distribution, IBCA said.
"Overseas expansion remains cautionary, though the number of franchise outlets -- currently 20 -- has the potential to grow to around 100 by the end of the century," it said.

"Despite intense competition in the UK, core operations continue to demonstrate profitable growth, and in the absence of any marked change in strategy, the strength of the Next brand should ensure further advances in the next few years."
